title: iOS Knowledge
intro: Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit and the platform concepts I use day to day. Edit this file to update the page.

entries.title: ARC and retain cycles
entries.summary: Automatic Reference Counting frees objects when strong references drop to zero. Closures and delegates are the usual cycle sources.
body: Use `weak` for back-references such as a delegate, and `[weak self]` in escaping closures that capture self.
`unowned` is safe only when the referenced object is guaranteed to outlive the reference.

entries.title: Value types vs reference types
entries.summary: Structs and enums are copied on assignment; classes share one instance.
body: Prefer structs for models and state snapshots. Use classes when identity or shared mutable state is required.

entries.title: async / await and actors
entries.summary: Structured concurrency replaces nested completion handlers. Actors serialize access to mutable state.
body: Mark UI-facing types with `@MainActor` so state changes happen on the main thread.

entries.title: State and property wrappers
entries.summary: @State owns local value state, @Binding borrows it, @StateObject owns a reference model, @ObservedObject borrows one.
body: Use `@StateObject` when the view creates the model, and `@ObservedObject` when a parent passes it in.
